subsystems.name: Algorithmic circuit layer
subsystems.role: defines exactly which quantum circuit is being costed.
parts: Shor's algorithm for factoring or discrete log
elliptic-curve point addition for ECC targets

subsystems.name: Error-correction model
subsystems.role: turns a list of logical gates into a repeating physical cycle.
parts: surface code or similar code family
code distance chosen against a physical error rate

subsystems.name: Non-Clifford resource model
subsystems.role: accounts for the expensive T-gates that carry the arithmetic.
parts: magic state distillation or cultivation factories

subsystems.name: Hardware assumption set
subsystems.role: the physical parameters the whole estimate is scaled to.
parts: physical gate and measurement error rate

subsystems.name: Accounting engine
subsystems.role: combines circuit, code and hardware into a space-time volume.

subsystems.name: Interpretation layer
subsystems.role: converts a number into a security conclusion.
parts: attacker-model assumptions such as parallel speed-ups

buildSteps.title: Fix the target and attacker model
buildSteps.detail: Choose the key size and scheme (for example RSA-2048 or a 256-bit elliptic-curve key), decide whether the attacker is a single machine, and state what classical pre- and post-processing is allowed.

buildSteps.title: Write the quantum circuit
buildSteps.detail: Build the arithmetic explicitly — modular exponentiation with windowed multiplication and compressed registers, or windowed elliptic-curve addition — and minimise its gate and qubit counts on paper.

buildSteps.title: Pick the fault-tolerance scheme
buildSteps.detail: Select a code such as the surface code, set lattice-surgery operations as the logical instruction set, and choose the code distance that suppresses logical errors below the target for the assumed physical error rate.

buildSteps.title: Count the non-Clifford cost
buildSteps.detail: Tally how many T-gates the circuit needs and how many magic states per second a distillation or cultivation factory can supply, since this usually sets the machine's size and speed.

buildSteps.title: Lay out the machine
buildSteps.detail: Place data-qubit patches, routing space and factories on a 2D grid, then trade qubit count against runtime — a bigger machine with more factories runs the same circuit faster.

buildSteps.title: Compute the space-time volume
buildSteps.detail: Multiply qubits by cycle time by number of cycles to get physical qubits and wall-clock hours, and report the pair rather than a single figure.

buildSteps.title: Stress-test the assumptions
buildSteps.detail: Re-run the model across a range of physical error rates, cycle times and algorithmic optimisations, and add margin for techniques not yet invented.

buildSteps.title: Translate into guidance
buildSteps.detail: Turn the range into exposure windows — data encrypted today and stored can be decrypted later — and compare against the migration schedule implied by post-quantum standards.

prerequisites.tech: Shor's algorithm and quantum arithmetic circuits
prerequisites.why: the circuit being costed has to exist before anything can be counted.

prerequisites.tech: Quantum error correction theory (surface codes, lattice surgery)
prerequisites.why: it is the factory model that converts noisy physical qubits into reliable logical ones.
it supplies the non-Clifford gates and often dominates the estimate, but is not yet run at useful scale.

prerequisites.tech: Classical simulation and benchmarking of error-corrected circuits
prerequisites.why: small instances are simulated to sanity-check the analytic models.

prerequisites.tech: A fault-tolerant quantum computer of the estimated size
prerequisites.why: without one, the estimates remain predictions that cannot be validated end to end.

pathway.milestone: published point estimates — for example roughly 20 million noisy qubits running for about eight hours for RSA-2048 (Gidney and Ekerå, 2021), with later work trading longer runtimes for fewer than a million qubits
pathway.unlocks: concrete deadlines in post-quantum migration policy, alongside standards finalised in 2024.

pathway.milestone: common reporting conventions and shared tooling, so competing estimates use the same attacker model and metrics
pathway.unlocks: estimates that can be compared directly instead of argued over.

pathway.milestone: estimates driven by measured hardware parameters rather than assumed ones
pathway.unlocks: shrinking error bars and earlier, better-founded migration dates.

pathway.milestone: a small cryptographic key broken on real error-corrected hardware
pathway.unlocks: the endpoint of the analysis becomes an engineering problem rather than a research question.

pathway.milestone: routines folded into cryptographic-agility practice and standards cycles
pathway.unlocks: key sizes and algorithms updated on a schedule, not in a panic.
